🔥🇲🇽 <u>Cerimedo's Network Runs Through the PRI and Claudio X's Sí por México</u>

A new Contralínea investigation traces Fernando Cerimedo's Miami-based disinformation network into Mexico's opposition: the PRI leadership and Sí por México, the platform bankrolled by Kimberly-Clark shareholder Claudio X. González that backed Xóchitl Gálvez.

The thread also reaches Alonso Cedeño, who shares stages with Dick Morris, "the mind behind the slogan 'López Obrador is a danger to Mexico'" in 2006. Cerimedo, Milei's former adviser and co-owner of La Derecha Diario, now faces prosecution in Bolivia for attempted femicide and money laundering.

🇲🇽🇨🇺 <u>Havana Salutes Morena at 15</u>

Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel congratulated Mexico's governing party on its 15th anniversary: "Our sincere congratulations to Morena for the 15 years of its foundation. We reiterate from the Communist Party of Cuba the commitment to continue deepening the ties of friendship and cooperation between our political organizations."

Morena was founded as a civil association on October 2, 2011, the anniversary of Tlatelolco, and won registration as a national party in 2014. Fifteen years later it governs Mexico, while Washington tightens the blockade on the island.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Operación Enjambre Hits Chiapas: Morena Mayor and Ex-Mayor Arrested</u>

Mexico's federal anti-corruption sweep just took down its own party's people. At 5:30 a.m. Saturday, federal forces arrested Suchiapa mayor Jorge Lara Cordero and former mayor Alexis Nucamendi, both from Morena, along with 19 others, including municipal police commanders and judicial staff.

The Security Cabinet says all 21 are under investigation for abuse of authority, corruption and criminal association. The raid comes days after the town's police director was detained over a prisoner's escape.

🇲🇽✊ "For thirty-six years they said that if the minimum wage went up there would be inflation… Between President López Obrador and us, the minimum wage has gone up 154 percent in real terms." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Vivienda para el Bienestar, Tejería, Veracruz The minimum wage was 2,800 pesos a month in 2018. Today it is more than 9,500. The Constitution now requires every government to raise it above the previous year's inflation. Higher wages also capitalized Infonavit and IMSS, which receive a share of payroll, and that money now funds 1.2 million homes this term and new hospital beds.

text: 🔥🇲🇽 "He had already paid 225,000 pesos and he owed 1,200,000 pesos. Can you believe it? Pure robbery, pure plunder. Do you know how much he owes now? Nothing." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Vivienda para el Bienestar, Tejería, Veracruz Leobardo had borrowed 67,000 pesos from Infonavit. Infonavit found 4,856,000 "unpayable" loans issued under neoliberal governments, whose balances grew even as borrowers kept paying. All of them have now been restructured, 200,000 of them in Veracruz. Another 150,000 paid-off Veracruz mortgages are being released free of charge. The registry procedure used to cost 16,000 to 18,000 pesos.

🇲🇽✊ "Governments must procure the happiness of the people. And what greater happiness than handing over the key to a home of their own to families of limited means in our country." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Vivienda para el Bienestar, Tejería, Veracruz She was quoting Morelos, whose Sentimientos de la Nación also called for moderating "opulence and indigence." The quote came as she handed over 900 homes at Infonavit Tejería in the port of Veracruz, the largest single handover of the Vivienda para el Bienestar program, which is now 43% complete nationwide. Infonavit's goal is 1.2 million homes this term: 60 m², two bedrooms, near hospitals, schools and transport. In Veracruz its goal was raised from 31,000 to 60,000 homes for workers earning under three minimum wages.

🇲🇽🚆 "We can say: campaign promise — fulfilled!" — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, inauguration of the Port of Veracruz access bridge The 2 km, 860-million-peso access bridge to the Port of Veracruz was due to open in December and opened on October 3 because the builder finished early. It is one of 400 bridges planned this term: rebuilds of bridges brought down by rain or other natural events, plus city access bridges, interchanges and tunnels to relieve traffic congestion. It serves people in the Veracruz metro area and the freight traffic headed to the port.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Sugar Imports Up 1,542%: Mexico Tightens the Gate</u>

Mexico's Economy Ministry is adding import permits for sugar-based food preparations after sugar imports jumped 1,542% between 2023 and 2025, from an average of 2,185 to 35,872 tonnes a month, El Financiero reports. The permit for tariff line 2106.90.99 was due on September 28 and now takes effect on November 2. It comes on top of the tariffs imposed in November 2025: up to 156% on sugar, and 210.44% on some liquid and invert sugars.
